💡 How to read this: a higher percentile means gold is more "expensive" relative to the model-implied equilibrium level.
- 1Y percentile: short-term sentiment (fast-moving variable)
- 3Y percentile: medium-term valuation position (shown in the charts)
- 10Y percentile: the core window used by the strategies
- All-history percentile: long-cycle conditions (slow-moving variable)
- Dual Product: 1Y percentile × all-history percentile; an exploratory signal. See "What Is the Dual Product?" below
Percentile bands: >90% (Extremely Overvalued) | 70%–90% (Overvalued) | 30%–70% (Fair Value) | 10%–30% (Undervalued) | <10% (Extremely Undervalued).

🔬 What Is the "Dual Product"? (Click to Expand/Collapse)
① Definition
Dual Product = 1Y percentile × all-history percentile

Example: 1Y percentile = 0.333, all-history percentile = 0.688 → Dual Product = 0.229

② Motivation
All strategies based on the 10Y percentile use only a single time scale (a rolling 10-year window). A natural question is whether signals from both the 1Y window (short-term sentiment) and all-history window (long-term valuation) can produce a more robust assessment. The "Dual Product" is an exploratory response to this question.
③ Design Logic

Both percentiles high → classify as overvalued only when short- and long-term signals confirm one another;
Both percentiles low → classify as undervalued only when both are low.

④ Three Limitations
⚠️ Limitation 1 (Scale): A percentile is the historical rank of a residual. Rank × rank is not a rank; the product is no longer a percentile.
⚠️ Limitation 2 (Left-Skewed Distribution): Multiplying two numbers in [0,1] pushes the result toward 0. For example, 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25, which shifts a "Fair Value" reading to "Extremely Undervalued" and can systematically inflate position size.
⚠️ Limitation 3 (Conflicting Signals): If the 1Y percentile indicates undervaluation (0.1) while the all-history percentile indicates overvaluation (0.9), their product is 0.09 and may still be classified as "Extremely Undervalued," prompting leverage in a contradictory signal environment.
⑤ Current Reading
1Y percentile = 0.333, all-history percentile = 0.688, Dual Product = 0.229.
For comparison, the 10Y percentile is 0.690 (at the lower boundary of the "Extremely Overvalued" range), while the Dual Product value of 0.229 falls in the "Fair Value" range. The two readings differ by a factor of 10, directly illustrating the Dual Product’s left-skew problem.
⑥ Conclusion

The Dual Product is retained as a methodological comparison to document the exploration of multi-timescale signal fusion. For academic comparison only; not a basis for trading decisions.

📉 Strategy Backtest and Return Performance

The backtest begins after the SGE benchmark was launched (2016-04-18 onward). All strategies use the previous day’s valuation percentile to determine the current day’s position, avoiding look-ahead information. A one-way transaction cost of 0.1% and an annual financing cost of 4.5% on position exposure above 1.0 are included. Each strategy uses its own exhaustively selected rebalancing threshold (see below).
📌 Note: All strategies and backtest results below are presented for model research only and do not constitute investment advice or trading instructions.

📐 Piecewise Position Function H(q)

Input: valuation percentile q. Output: position-function value before applying the position cap.
q < 0.1(Extremely Undervalued): Position = 3.0 - 5.0 × q　→ 2.5 ~ 3.0
0.1 ≤ q < 0.3(Undervalued): Position = 2.5 - 5.0 × (q - 0.1)　→ 1.5 ~ 2.5
0.3 ≤ q < 0.7(Fair Value): Position = 1.5 - 2.5 × (q - 0.3)　→ 0.5 ~ 1.5
0.7 ≤ q < 0.9(Overvalued): Position = 0.5 - 2.0 × (q - 0.7)　→ 0.1 ~ 0.5
q ≥ 0.9(Extremely Overvalued): Position = 0.1　→ reduce to the minimum position

Design principle: the function assigns larger positions in undervalued ranges and smaller positions in overvalued ranges. Breakpoints 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.7 / 0.9 define five valuation bands. Strategies differ in the position cap (1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0).

🎯 Strategy-Specific Rebalancing Thresholds (Exhaustively Selected)

Rebalancing threshold: rebalancing is triggered only when the difference between the target and current positions exceeds the threshold. A larger threshold means lower turnover and lower costs; a smaller threshold tracks signals more closely but increases turnover. Based on the Pareto-optimal results from an exhaustive search of 9,400 combinations, this dashboard assigns a separate threshold to each strategy:

Consequently, if the valuation percentile remains in the same range for an extended period, some strategies may show no rebalancing records for weeks or months. This is an expected feature of the low-turnover design, not missing data.

📌 Rebalancing schedule: - daily: rebalance every trading day using the previous day’s percentile - weekly: rebalance each Friday (skip the week if Friday is not a trading day), using the previous day’s percentile - monthly: rebalance on the last trading day of each month (day must be >= 25), using the previous day’s percentile - quarterly: rebalance on the last trading day of each quarter-end month (March/June/September/December; day must be >= 25) - On non-rebalancing days, the previous position is maintained, with no transaction costs incurred

💡 Frequency trade-off: for 10Y Smart 3.0, the daily version has an annualized return of 25.7% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.25; the weekly version has an annualized return of 22.8% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.13; the monthly version has an annualized return of 21.4% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.09. Lower-frequency versions use fewer trades and incur lower transaction costs while retaining broadly similar return–risk characteristics.

📊 Gold and Factor Relationships

📌 Figure 1: Over the past decade, gold has risen from around US$1,200 to approximately US$4147. The current rolling 3-year percentile is 73.3%, in the Overvalued range. Recent central-bank net gold purchases are around 47.6 tonnes per month.

📌 Figure 2: Current TIPS yield: 2.88%; China–US yield spread: -3.54%. Latest gold/oil ratio: 44.2.

📊 Residual Series

📌 Figure 3: The current residual is 0.0612, in the Fair Value range.

🧠 Model Interpretation

Regression equation: Ln(Gold) = 7.3932 + -0.3000×TIPS + -31.6868×CN_US_Spread + 0.0110×Gold_Oil_Ratio, R²=0.913

Factor definitions:

  • TIPS (US 10-year real yield): measures the opportunity cost of holding gold. Higher TIPS yields tend to pressure gold; the estimated coefficient is negative.
  • China–US yield spread (CN_US_Spread): China’s 10-year government-bond yield minus the US 10-year Treasury yield; intended to capture capital-allocation dynamics between China and the US.
  • Gold/oil ratio (Gold_Oil_Ratio): the price ratio of gold to WTI crude oil, reflecting safe-haven sentiment and relative valuation.

Duration of extreme-overvaluation episodes: Extremely overvalued in 26 episode(s); average duration 10 trading days, maximum 82 trading days

Residual percentile: the current residual is 0.0612, in the Fair Value range.
